title: Replay4NCL: An Efficient Memory Replay-based Methodology for Neuromorphic Continual Learning in Embedded AI Systems
problem: Neuromorphic continual learning (NCL) with SNNs faces significant latency and energy overhead from memory replay techniques that rely on long timesteps and compression-decompression cycles, making them unsuitable for embedded AI systems like mobile robots and edge agents.
motivation: Embedded AI systems demand energy-efficient and low-latency learning; current SNN replay methods incur prohibitive overheads that prevent practical deployment in resource-constrained environments.
method: Replay4NCL compresses latent data (old knowledge) and replays it with reduced timesteps during NCL training to minimize latency and energy. The approach compensates for information loss from spike reduction by dynamically adjusting neuron threshold potential and learning rate settings to preserve accuracy.
key_novelty: Combination of latent data compression with threshold and learning-rate adaptation during replay to maintain knowledge retention while drastically reducing timesteps and energy cost.
contributions: 90.43% top-1 accuracy in class-incremental scenarios, outperforming baseline 86.22%
20% latent memory savings and 36.43% energy reduction
Practical method for enabling NCL in embedded systems without sacrificing accuracy
limitations: Evaluation limited to Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD) dataset; scalability to larger, more complex datasets not addressed.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient neuromorphic continual learning for embedded systems
